about: measure contests of 2024 in Idaho, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds (D3). Built by pipeline/local_medsl.py from pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py's cache.

medsl.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, Precinct-Level Returns 2024 by Individual State, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/NYTPDU, version 1.0
medsl.note: precinct returns compiled by MEDSL from each state's official sources (named per state in its README); added up to the contest by pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py, files 2024-id-precinct-general.csv

model.name: the model's own forecast, method D3-v1.1
model.note: each year forecast from a fit on earlier years only; no polls are used

nara.name: National Archives, Electoral College Results (the sitting president's party)
nara.licence: US federal public record; no licence printed

klarner.name: Carl Klarner, State Legislative Election Returns, 1967-2022, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/FJOGJB, v1.0, released 2024-06-12T21:56:14Z (the races route (a) is fitted on)

census_places.name: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census: national_place_by_county2020.txt (each place once for each county it lies in; codes2020 reference files)
census_places.licence: a work of the U.S. Government (17 U.S.C. 105); no licence printed

census_cousub.name: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census: national_cousub2020.txt (each county subdivision with its county; codes2020 reference files): towns and townships with a government of their own (FUNCSTAT A), which nest within their county, and the names that are both a place's and a subdivision's
census_cousub.licence: a work of the U.S. Government (17 U.S.C. 105); no licence printed

question.title: Constitutional Amendment Hjr 5

p.not_computed: Idaho Const. art. XX, §1: majority of 'the electors'; denominator not stated in the text I read: the threshold turns on more than the yes share of those voting on the question, and the model forecasts that share only

question.title: Proposition 1

source.name: Idaho Secretary of State: 2024 Idaho Voter Pamphlet, General Election November 5, 2024 (linked from voteidaho.gov/initiatives-amendments, saved at id_init_amend.html)

ballot_text.source_title: Proposition One: Idaho Open Primaries Act (Measure to: (1) replace voter selection of party nominees with a top-four primary; (2) require a ranked-choice voting system for general elections)
ballot_text.type_quote: Full Text of Proposed Law for Proposition One

fact.quote: The proposition proposes to modify existing law. Each section of the proposition will amend existing code sections, propose new code sections, or repeal code sections.
fact.why: The pamphlet calls the measure 'the initiative' ('The initiative creates a system where all candidates participate in a top-four primary'), prints its 'Full Text of Proposed Law' headed 'Be it enacted by the People of Idaho', and its sections amend Idaho Code. It is a statutory initiative. The same pamphlet also prints a separate 'Proposed Constitutional Amendment', which is not 'Proposition One' and not in our list.

source.name: Idaho Secretary of State: 2024 Idaho Voter Pamphlet, General Election November 5, 2024 (linked from voteidaho.gov/initiatives-amendments, saved at id_init_amend.html)

threshold.rule: majority of those voting on the measure (statute; Const. art. III, §1 leaves conditions to the legislature)
threshold.quote: declaring such measures as are approved by a majority of those voted thereon to be in full force and effect as the law of the state of Idaho
threshold.matched: by the type the ballot text states (statute; data/measure/ballot-texts.json)

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures
p.note: this route's back-test of statewide measures shows more near-even finishes than it forecast (12 against 9.1 within 1 point of ½, and 11 against 6.9 within 20,000 votes, 2018 to 2024), so p may be low
